article.headline: Cheniere Rises 2% A Day After FERC Approves Sabine Pass Expansion
article.deck: Back above the 300.99 buy point of a 30-week cup after a bounce off the 50-day line, in range up to 316.04.
body: Cheniere Energy rose 5.98, or 2.0%, to 301.99, closing just above the 300.99 buy point of a 30-week cup. The base ran from a March 30 high to a June 18 low and corrected 25.7%. The buy range runs to 316.04, and the close sits 0.3% past the buy point. Volume was 0.69x the 50-day average.

The stock broke out Oct. 29 on 2.47x average volume, 19 sessions ago, then slipped back to its 50-day line. Today's gain was a bounce off that line: the close is 4.9% above the 50-day at 287.94 and 1.6% above the 21-day at 297.17, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, meaning the session traded through it. The stock is 8.7% below its 52-week high of 330.73. It ranks 90 of 99 on the desk's list, though the RS line sits 9.8% under its high. Shares are up 55.4% this year.

In the September quarter Cheniere earned 5.65 a share, up 18.9% from a year earlier, on revenue of $6.17 billion, up 39.0%. Earlier quarters swung widely, from 14.65 a share in June to a loss of 16.65 in March, so the earnings line is uneven. The stock trades at 13.13 times forward earnings, with a market cap of $61.7 billion.

IntelliNews reported Tuesday that FERC approved the Sabine Pass LNG Stage 5 expansion project. Zacks headlines on Tuesday and Wednesday tied energy stocks to supply disruptions and gas funds to colder weather.
A close back under 300.99 would stall the breakout again; a close under the 50-day line would undo the bounce.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds above the 300.99 buy point and the 287.94 50-day line.

article.headline: Disney Climbs 2.5% To New High As Quarterly Profit More Than Doubles
article.deck: Five sessions past the 119.88 buy point of a 62-week cup, Disney closed at 125.60, inside a buy range that ends at 125.87.
body: Disney rose 3.09, or 2.5%, to 125.60 and hit a new high, five sessions after breaking out of a 62-week cup. The base corrected 23.0% from an Aug. 22, 2025, high to a March 27 low of 92.19. The buy point is 119.88 and the buy range ends at 125.87; the close is 4.8% past the buy point, near the top of the range. Volume ran 1.76x the 50-day average.

The breakout came Nov. 18 on 2.02x average volume. The close sits 0.5% under the 52-week high of 126.28, 6.4% above the 21-day line at 118.02 and 12.6% above the 50-day at 111.51. That is 0.92 ATRs from the 21-day line, an intact trend rather than a stretched one. The RS line hit a new high, and the stock ranks 91 of 99 on the desk's list. Disney is up 13.9% in a month and 10.4% this year.

In the September quarter Disney earned 1.51 a share, up 106.8% from a year earlier, on revenue of $25.95 billion, up 15.5%. Per-share earnings matched the June quarter's 1.51 and topped the 1.27 and 1.34 of the two quarters before. Next earnings are due Feb. 1. The stock trades at 14.65 times forward earnings, with a market cap of $214.5 billion.

The day's headlines were not about the business: Investor's Business Daily ran an options piece on the dividend, and the Wall Street Journal ran a story on the friendship breakup behind Bob Iger's biggest boardroom fight.
A close above 125.87 would take Disney out of the buy range; a slip back under 119.88 would mark a stalled breakout.
article.watch: The 125.87 top of the buy range: a close above it leaves the stock extended.

article.deck: The day-old breakout from an 11-week flat base closed in range at 564.12, but the after-hours price of 520.50 is under the 560.35 buy point and the 50-day line.
body: Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell 43.62, or 7.7%, to 520.50 after hours as of 5:38 p.m. Eastern, after a Stocktwits headline said the FDA delayed its decision on a kidney drug and rival VERA surged. At the close the stock was up 0.20 at 564.12, 0.7% past the 560.35 buy point of an 11-week flat base, one session after breaking out. Regular-session volume was 1.18x the 50-day average.

The after-hours price sits below the buy point, below the 21-day line at 538.64 and below the 50-day at 525.11. If it holds into the next session, the breakout becomes a stalled one. The base corrected 13.6% from a Sept. 3 high to an Oct. 13 low of 484.08; the buy range runs to 588.37. The breakout came Nov. 24 on 1.01x average volume. At the close the stock was 1.3% under its 52-week high of 571.75 and 0.7 ATRs from the 21-day line, with the RS line at a new high and a rank of 82 of 99 on the desk's list.

The September quarter showed earnings of 2.56 a share, down 39.0% from a year earlier, on revenue of $3.44 billion, up 11.8%. Per-share earnings slipped from 4.31 in the June quarter. Next earnings are due Feb. 11. The stock trades at 28.32 times forward earnings, with a market cap of $143.0 billion.
Earlier in the day the Motley Fool wrote that Vertex could land a fifth franchise on Nov. 30 when the FDA decides, and Simply Wall St. weighed a renewed drug discovery deal.
article.watch: Whether the next session opens under the 560.35 buy point and the 525.11 50-day line.

body: AbbVie develops, makes and sells prescription medicines worldwide. Its biggest franchises treat immune and inflammatory diseases, with Skyrizi and Rinvoq, and blood cancers, with Imbruvica and Venclexta; newer cancer drugs include Elahere, Epkinly and Emrelis. It also runs an aesthetics business built on facial injectables, body contouring and skincare.

The stock fell 5.80, or 1.9%, to 294.48 on Wednesday, on volume 1.2x its 50-day average, and was little changed after hours at 293.80. It sits 2.8% under its 52-week high of 302.98 and is up 28.9% this year and 28.3% over 12 months.

The quarters show a recovery. Per-share earnings went from 1.02 in the December 2025 quarter to 0.39 in March, then 2.03 in June and 2.37 in September. The September figure was up 2270.0% from a year earlier, a jump off a very small base, so revenue is the cleaner read: $17.40 billion, up 10.3%, after $15.00 billion in March and $16.99 billion in June.
The market values AbbVie at $520.5 billion. It trades at 50.60 times trailing earnings but 18.16 times forward earnings; the trailing figure still carries the weak earlier quarters.

AbbVie broke out Oct. 7 from a 10-week flat base that corrected 9.8% from a July 29 high to an Aug. 6 low of 241.20. The buy point was 267.57 and the buy range ran to 280.95; breakout volume was 1.29x average. Thirty-five sessions later the stock is 10.1% past the buy point, extended, and the entry is gone until a new base forms or the stock pulls back to a moving average. It sits 1.6% above the 21-day line at 289.87, 0.52 ATRs from it, and 4.8% above the 50-day at 280.92, near the top of the old buy range. It ranks 87 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 1.7% off its high.

Health care is the desk's strongest group, with an average RS of 72 and 76% of its 17 names above their 50-day lines. A GuruFocus headline on Tuesday tied that day's gain to a health care rally as tech slid, and Barron's on Wednesday called AbbVie a pharma stock for shelter from the AI storm. Next earnings are due Feb. 3.
article.watch: A pullback toward the 50-day line at 280.92 or a new base would set up the next entry.

chief.verdict: The leadership is defensive and thin: the names actually in buy range are Cheniere, Disney, Amgen, Apple and Vertex, while ai chips have 0% of their names above the 50-day and ai infra carries an average RS of 21. Healthcare leads the groups at an average RS of 72 with 76% above the 50-day. Even that group got a warning after the bell, when Vertex fell 7.7% to 520.5 on an FDA delay. The risk leans down: the Nasdaq is 9.2% below its 50-day and 14.9% off its high, and new breakouts are coming on light or average volume.
chief.market: With the market in correction and 10 distribution days on the S&P 500 (weighted 9.8) and 9 on the Nasdaq (9.8), keep exposure small: one or two half positions at most, and cut any that slip back under the buy point.

picks.why: This is the cleanest chart on the desk. It is a 30-week cup, 25.7% deep, that broke out on 2.47 times normal volume on 2026-10-29, came back and has now bounced off the 50-day line at 287.94 to close at 301.99, just 0.3% over the 300.99 buy point. Earnings are behind it, and the energy group news is supportive. The risk is that today's 2.0% gain came on 0.69 times average volume, so nobody big has confirmed the bounce yet.
picks.entry: 300.99 to 316.04. Confirm with a close above 301 on above-average volume. Get out on a close back below the 50-day at 287.94.

picks.why: This is the best base on the board: a 62-week cup, 23.0% deep, that broke out on 2.02 times volume on 2026-11-18, with the RS line at a new high and earnings growth of 106.8%. But it closed at 125.6, 4.8% over the 119.88 buy point, just under the 125.87 top of the range and 12.6% above its 50-day. Chasing it here means buying at the top of the range.
picks.entry: Buy a pullback toward the 21-day EMA at 118.02 that holds the 119.88 buy point. Don't pay more than 125.87.

picks.why: This is the one aggressive early entry worth starting. It is a 26-week cup with RS 92, closing at 131.94, 2.5% under the 135.26 buy point, in a megacap group where 45% of the names hold their 50-day. A defensive leader is the right kind of name to lean on in a correction. The risk is that the market drags it back into the base before it clears the pivot.
picks.entry: A small starter near 131.94. Add only on a move through 135.26 on strong volume, and keep the full position under 142.02.

picks.why: It is a tight 12-week flat base, only 10.6% deep, that broke out on 1.48 times volume on 2026-11-04 and has pulled back to 52.93, 0.2% under the 53.02 buy point, holding the 50-day at 51.86. RS 75 is only middling for a leader, and the stock trades at a trailing P/E of 43.
picks.entry: A close back above 53.02 on above-average volume reopens the buy, up to 55.67. A close under the 50-day at 51.86 ends it.

avoid.why: The flat-base breakout over 560.35 came on only 1.01 times volume, and after hours the stock fell 7.7% to 520.5 on an FDA delay, well back below the buy point. Earnings were also down 39.0%.
RS 99, but it closed 17.6% under the 432.43 buy point and slid 4.0% to 341.9 after hours, leaving it 20.9% below the pivot. That is too far away to start an aggressive entry.
It is a 57-week deep cup in a recent-IPO group with an average RS of 31. That is a technically valid base but too loose and too long to trust in a correction, even 5.1% from the 24.1 buy point.
Earnings land in 5 days on 2026-11-30, and the stock sits 22.9% below its 140.02 buy point and 6.9% under its 50-day, so there is no setup to own through the report.

chief.watch: Whether LNG can hold above its 300.99 buy point on rising volume. If even the cleanest bounce on the desk fails, it is time to go to cash.
